sections.title: What is an Expert Opinion Letter?
sections.html:
Expert Opinion Letter (EOL), aka Professional Experience Evaluation, is written by university professors or experts to pair your relevant professional experience with academic coursework to determine a U.S. degree equivalency.

It's widely used for Eb1a, Eb2-NIW, H1B (or H1B RFE), TN-Visa and other immigration related cases.

Contact us for a Free Estimate!

sections.title: Why do you need an Expert Opinion Letter?
sections.html:
You may need to request this service because:
1. You dont't have a four-year bachelor's degree (for H1B) or a master's degree (for Eb1a, Eb2) in your home country
2. You have many years of work experience in your field
3. You're applying for Eb1a, Eb2, H1B, TN-Visa, and other immigration-related cases
4. USCIS needs a proof that you have a US equivalent advanced degree.

Contact us for a Free Estimate!

sections.title: 3 Easy Steps for Expert Opinion Letters
sections.html:
Order your Expert Opinion Letter in 3 easy steps:
1. Click here to fill out the Application Form.
2. Choose your turnaround time and pricing accordingly in the Form.
3. Email the completed form and other required documents to AET:
Miami Office, San Francisco Office, Boston Office, Los Angeles Office or New York Office.

Please note, required documents typically include 3 of the following:

  • Evidence of receipt of lesser nationally or internationally recognized prizes or awards for excellence;
  • Evidence of membership in associations in the field which demand outstanding achievement of their members (not the typical professional association);
  • Evidence of published material about the applicant in professional or major trade publications or other major media (media mentions)
  • Evidence that the applicant has been asked to judge the work of others, either individually or on a panel
  • Evidence of original scientific, scholarly, artistic, athletic, or business-related contributions of major significance to the field
  • Evidence of the applicant's authorship of scholarly articles in professional or major trade publications or other major media
  • Evidence of the applicant's performance of a leading or critical role in distinguished organizations
  • Evidence that the applicant commands a high salary or other significantly high remuneration in relation to others in the field
